status: in progress; throughput and memory parity remain unmet
acceptance: Keep pursuing throughput and memory parity before accepting the pivot.
implementation: The reliable record assembler uses a Vec with explicit geometric reserve_exact growth capped at the announced record size. It retains staged 4096-byte reads, pre-allocation admission, the existing two-times-size read lease for growth/transient headroom, and immutable Bytes ownership after assembly. No framing, limits, delivery, FIFO, deadline, crypto or congestion-control changes.
tradeoffs: Large records no longer request the next power-of-two capacity beyond their announced size. This still allocates and copies incoming bytes; it is not a zero-copy decoder. Small records below the existing 4096-byte staging size have the same requested initial capacity. RSS remains allocator/workload dependent; capacity diagnostics are separate from process RSS.
scope: Local Linux loopback; ordinary release builds and frozen verifying clients. Three alternating fresh-process repetitions per case/variant, no concurrent build/test/browser during timing. Four pinned server workers on CPUs 0-3, eight pinned client workers on CPUs 8-15, four seconds; main screen uses 1 KiB values, 32 private pairs, 1024 room readers, fanout window four. Large private screens use 64 KiB with 32 pairs and 1 MiB with four pairs. Capacity uses 100000 independently counted physical QUIC connections, eight server workers on CPUs 0-7, four offered seconds and 400000 exactly verified deliveries. Logarithmic latency percentiles are upper bounds. RSS is sampled at phase gates, excludes kernel socket memory and differs from continuous peak or requested live heap.

capacity_layout.scope: Independent allocation-capacity diagnostic mirrors the two actual growth loops at representative complete record sizes. It measures requested collection capacity, not complete live heap, allocation count or process RSS. Whole-operation benchmark data is separate.

research_leads.scope: Read-only upstream research; no dependency changes and no causal conclusion for this branch. Investigate with a local reproducer/profile before implementing. The dedup report targets another deployment/version; current pinned source independently still uses u128 at connection/spaces.rs:480.

validation.vendor: 152 files verified against four original archives and three declared patches; dependencies unchanged
validation.browser: Chromium 155 actual delivered bundle, all nine checks passed: three sessions, typed broadcast, cross-room private, datagrams, 128 KiB/5 MiB values, concurrent variables, unsafe-number rejection, departure and genuine graceful closure. Seven final gauges zero.
validation.write_deadline_regression: Real independent wtransport client: 64 KiB stream receive credit, unread 12 MiB private delivery exceeding the default 10 MB transport send window. Write timeout increments exactly once, queued/read budget credit releases, another room remains responsive before and after timeout, and shutdown clears connection/output metadata credit. Current full suite passed. This is the unchanged existing regression, rerun in the current full suite.

historical_controls.scope: Previously measured controls, not rerun during this checkpoint. Plaintext remains the existing parity baseline. The encrypted fixture includes both proxy and backend CPU/RSS and an additional loopback hop; it is not a native-WSS performance ceiling.

freshness_scope: One candidate regression sample per clean/loss/reordering mode; 360 offered 1 KiB states at 60 Hz over six seconds with concurrent reliable 1 MiB bulk. Loss: 20 ms one-way and 2% packet loss; reordering adds 8 ms jitter and 25% reorder. Both directions, external port only, temporary isolated namespace, TLS fixture internal hop unimpaired. Matching seeds/parameters do not impose identical packet-loss trajectories. Probes include initial state before first update; stale sequences never replace fresh state. Missing means unreceived observations, not all attributed to network loss. No statistical protocol ranking is claimed.
remaining: Large-record requested capacity and 1 MiB workload RSS improve, but small-message reliable throughput and 100k RSS are essentially unchanged. Overall throughput and memory parity remain unmet against the earlier plaintext control; mixed private traffic also trails the earlier encrypted fixture. Continue active QUIC/HTTP3 storage, receive framing and reliable scheduling. Locally measure the upstream reordering-window report before attributing bulk stalls to it. Full observer cancellation/re-subscribe, concurrent 100k/8192 inspection, broader overload/shutdown/retirement fallback, QUIC buffer accounting and final packaging/deployment documentation remain required. No acceptance or release claim.
